items.htmltext: Presenting “Racialized Language in Criminal Courtrooms” at the Law and Society Association Annual Conference (May 2026).
Presented “How Judicial Gender Composition Affects Sentencing Decisions: Evidence from Japanese Criminal Courts” at the 19th Annual Conference on Empirical Legal Studies (CELS).
Began work as a Research Assistant on the Larry P. v. Riles Project with Prof. Alfredo Artiles and Prof. Bill Koski.
Named Pre-doctoral Fellow at the Walter H. Shorenstein Asia-Pacific Research Center (APARC), Freeman Spogli Institute, Stanford.
Named Digital Humanities Research Scholar at the Center for Spatial and Textual Analysis (CESTA), Stanford.

Presented “Female Voice in the Courtroom” at the Trans-Altai Sustainability Dialogue, Gender Equality, co-hosted by the Parliament of Mongolia, Stanford APARC, and the Ban Ki-moon Foundation For a Better Future.
Presented at the Salzburg Cutler Fellows Program on the effectiveness of labor provisions in trade agreements.
Admitted to the New York Bar.
